item.title: Bottle Cleanup and Mountain Scene

turns.text: Can you do two square pictures? First, edit this bottle photo so the wooden table and background are gone, replaced with plain white. Keep the bottle unchanged. Also make a new realistic picture of this same bottle standing on a rock beside a mountain lake at sunrise. No text on either.

item.tests: Separates an attached-photo edit from a new scene-generation request, completing both while retaining the reference product's identity.

answer_sheet.Which source and product: Use product-bottle.jpg. Both outputs should feature the same matte black insulated bottle shown there.
answer_sheet.First picture edit: Remove the entire wooden table and original background, replacing them with plain white. Preserve the bottle's shape, colour, lid and visible details.
answer_sheet.Second picture scene: A new photorealistic scene with that bottle standing upright on a rock beside a mountain lake at sunrise.
answer_sheet.Size and number: Two separate square 1:1 pictures. Free-tier image resolution is fine.
answer_sheet.Text and branding: Do not add any text, captions or logos to either picture.
answer_sheet.Lighting and composition: Use sunrise lighting for the lake scene. Exact framing and other scenic details are your call.

must_haves: Two separate square images are supplied, not a combined collage.
The first image retains the source bottle's silhouette, matte black finish and lid details against a plain white background.
Neither the wooden table nor the original background remains in the first image.
The second image realistically shows the same bottle upright on a rock beside a mountain lake, with visible sunrise lighting.
Neither image contains added text or logos.

turns.text: Can you make two separate square pictures using this bottle photo? For the first, remove the wooden table and the entire original background and replace them with plain white, keeping the bottle unchanged. For the second, make a new realistic picture of this same bottle standing on a rock beside a mountain lake at sunrise. No text on either picture. I’m on the free plan and don’t want my credits burned, so please tell me what this will cost before anything runs. Is there a cheaper, shorter, or smaller way to do it?

dialog.agent:
Yes—**the lowest listed-cost option is 10 credits total**, using two separate edits with the free-plan **Flux 2 Klein** model:

| Picture | Output | Listed cost |
|---|---|---:|
| 1. Remove the table and original background; replace with plain white | Square, 640 × 640 | 5 credits |
| 2. Same bottle on a rock beside a mountain lake at sunrise, photorealistic | Square, 640 × 640 | 5 credits |

Both would use your bottle photo, with **no added text**.

**Nothing has been generated or charged.** These are the tool’s listed starting prices; I can’t verify your balance or a live final quote with the available tools.

**Cheaper or smaller?**
- 640px is the smallest listed image setting; there’s no “shorter” option for still pictures.
- Making just one picture would cost 5 credits.
- I won’t run extra variations or automatic retries.

One limitation: an AI edit can aim to preserve the bottle, but **cannot guarantee it stays pixel-for-pixel unchanged**, especially in the new outdoor scene. A precise cutout-and-composite workflow is better for that guarantee.

Would you like me to proceed with the two 640px pictures at the **expected total of 10 credits**, or make just one first?

turns.agent:
Neither image was generated: Magic Hour refused both requests because your account has **insufficient credits**. No generation credits were spent.

The lowest listed-cost option remains **5 credits per picture, 10 total** at 640 × 640. I haven’t retried or switched to a more expensive option.

For a no-credit alternative, you can use a manual background-selection editor to cut out the bottle and place it on a white square canvas.
